chunks: And with this chain, from Salamah, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addab, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Khalid al-Qalanisi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Allah feels shy/ashamed to punish those who reach the age of eighty.

He (the Imam) said: An elderly man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and his book of deeds will be handed to him. Its outward appearance, regarding what is close to people, shows only his flaws/bad deeds. That will seem long to him, so he will say: 'O Lord! Will You return me to the Fire?'
The Almighty, Exalted is His Majesty, will say: 'O elderly! I feel shy to punish you, for you used to offer Salat for Me in the abode of the world. Go, take My servant to Paradise.'

key_terms.أَبْنَاءِ الثَّمَانِينَ: Those who reach the age of eighty
key_terms.يَسْتَحِي: To feel shy or modest (divine attribute)

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah feel shy to punish the elderly in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the concept of *istihya* (divine shyness/modesty) as a specific mechanism for the forgiveness of the elderly, emphasizing that reaching the age of eighty serves as a spiritual milestone. It illustrates the transition from fear of punishment to hope in mercy, where the physical act of Salat in the world acts as the decisive factor for entry into Paradise, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the cumulative weight of lifelong devotion.
